candidates.tagline: Apple's $1,999 foldable cracked after ~20 folds — the hinge was pressing into the screen
candidates.story: Reports flooded in on Oct 25–27, 2026 of Apple's first-ever foldable iPhone Duo developing cracks along the inner display's center fold within hours or days of purchase; iFixit's teardown found the hinge's central support bar may not drop far enough when opening, pressing directly against the flexible screen — Apple is now collecting affected units and charging $999 out-of-warranty for a screen replacement.
candidates.why_funny: Apple spent years insisting it needed to get foldable phones right before releasing one, then the hinge of its $1,999 debut foldable literally presses a support bar into the screen it's supposed to support.
candidates.alt: An open iPhone Duo foldable smartphone lying face-up on a wooden surface, showing a prominent crack running across the inner display along the center fold line

candidates.tagline: Apple's new desktop is roughly the size of a hardback book and costs as much as a Toyota Corolla
candidates.story: On October 28, 2026, Apple started selling the Mac Studio M5 Ultra with 512GB of unified RAM for $22,299 — or $29,799 with 16TB of storage; Macworld pointed out that buying two 256GB Mac Studios would give you the same total RAM, twice the storage, and two processors, for about $700 less.
candidates.why_funny: Apple put more RAM in a compact desktop than most cloud servers, priced it at new-car money, and the workaround to get the same specs cheaper is to buy two of them.
candidates.alt: An Apple Mac Studio silver compact desktop computer shown from the front with '512 GB' displayed in large overlaid text, and the Apple Mac Studio logo below
